title: Maximum Path Quality of a Graph
summary: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and an array of node values, find the maximum quality of a valid path that starts and ends at node 0 within maxTime seconds.
statement: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and an array of node values, find the maximum quality of a valid path that starts and ends at node 0 within maxTime seconds. The quality is the sum of unique node values visited. Each node can be visited multiple times, but each node's value is counted only once. There are at most four edges per node.
constraints: The undirected graph has nonnegative node values, positive edge times, and degree at most four.
A valid walk starts and ends at node zero within max_time; revisits are allowed but each node value counts once.
hints: The small time budget and degree bound permit enumerating feasible walks, while visit counts prevent duplicate value credit.
Depth-first search from zero, trying edges that fit; add a node value only on its first visit and update the answer only at zero.
Increment visits before recursion and decrement after; carry elapsed time and quality.
Every feasible walk is a DFS prefix, reversible visit counts exactly encode uniqueness, and only return-to-zero prefixes qualify for the maximum.
editorial: Every feasible walk is a DFS prefix, reversible visit counts exactly encode uniqueness, and only return-to-zero prefixes qualify for the maximum.

tests.explanation: Visiting nodes zero, one, and three while returning to zero yields quality seventy-five.
Only one branch can be visited and returned within time, so node three gives quality twenty-five.
